Subject: Request: temporary latency buffer & credit cap for PulseAI pilot

Sean —

Quick summary: PulseAI (PL-2027-048) is asking for a short-term latency tolerance and a capped service-credit remedy for a 3-month pilot. Their engineers are running a higher request fanout that increases p95/p99 by ~40% during specific batch ingestion windows. They want us to commit to the pilot on our standard pricing, but they require a narrower penalty exposure while they stabilize traffic.

What we propose (below) is a carveout so we can move fast and close the pilot this quarter. I need an executive thumbs-up to offer this to the customer (non-standard SLA terms + one-time onboarding credit) and permission to log a Deal Desk exception. Documents attached: PulseAI_SOW_v3.pdf and SLA-impact-analysis.xlsx.

Proposed exception (commercial + remedy):
- Temporary latency tolerance: 6 weeks from go-live where p99 may exceed our default latency SLO by up to 200ms during defined ingestion windows (00:00–06:00 PT). Outside windows standard SLOs apply.
- Service credit cap: monthly service-credit cap of 5% of monthly invoice for the duration of the tolerance period.
- One-time onboarding credit: $12,000 applied on first invoice.
- Contract term: pilot 3 months, auto-renew to month-to-month unless both sides sign full SOW.

Why: PulseAI is strategically important (AI-powered insights for a Fortune 200 partner) and the pilot has timing constraints tied to their Q2 rollout. Engineering has identified a mitigation plan (rate-limiting + prefix cache priming) that should reduce exposure after 6 weeks.

Asks:
1) Exec approval to offer the above exception and credit cap.
2) Legal (Lauren) to confirm contract language guardrails (audit right, expiration, revert to baseline SLOs).
3) Confirmation of the exact credit mechanics to include in the SOW (monetary cap vs. % credit).

Thanks — I can jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the concise ask and the analysis. I support making the pilot happen but want a tightened guardrail on the remedy side. A couple of points before I give formal sign-off: 

- Keep the tolerance window strictly scoped (both time of day and measured metric). We should document the exact aggregation method (rolling 5-minute p99) and the test harness they used.
- Prefer a monetary cap instead of only % credits — avoids surprises on large invoices. Suggest a 5% credit cap AND a hard monetary cap of $25k/month during the tolerance period.
- Limit exception duration to 6 weeks as proposed; include an automatic revert to baseline SLO at the end date unless both parties agree in writing to extend.
- Include an engineering checkpoint at week 3 (joint triage) with optional Redwood remediation support (billed separately).

If Lauren and Vivek are comfortable with the legal/technical side and the customer accepts the $25k monthly cap, you have my exec clearance to proceed and log the Deal Desk exception.

Please prepare a one-paragraph clause we can paste into the SOW.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts

Thanks — I like the structure. A few legal guardrails and recommended language below.

Key legal items:
- Duration: exception limited to a 6-week tolerance period starting on the agreed go-live date.
- Reversion: SLOs revert automatically at period end; any extension requires written approval executed by an authorized Redwood executive.
- Audit and data: Redwood will retain the right to access telemetry logs during the tolerance period for verification; we will not share customer PII.
- Customer remedies: propose both a % credit (5% of monthly invoice) and a monetary cap ($25,000/month) — whichever is lower. We should also tie credits to verified incidents only (post-triage).
- Termination: If the customer requests early termination of the pilot for performance reasons, they retain right to prorated credit for verified incidents through termination date.

Suggested SOW clause (one paragraph to paste):
"For an initial six-week tolerance period commencing on the agreed go-live date, Redwood will temporarily permit a defined latency tolerance for p99 latency during the daily ingestion window (00:00–06:00 PT). During this period, the customer's sole remedy for verified SLO violations shall be credited against monthly invoices at a rate not to exceed five percent (5%) of the monthly invoice or twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000), whichever is less. All credits require verification by Redwood engineering and are subject to the audit procedures set forth in Appendix A. The tolerance period will expire automatically unless extended by mutual written agreement of authorized representatives of both parties."

If that language looks good to Sean, I approve from Legal. Please add the audit appendix reference and loop in Contracts to place the clause in the SOW.

—Lauren
